children: His Mother Made Him a Coat From Cleaning Rags
Mike’s mother worried that her teenage son would be cold in America. So, using cleaning rags and knitting materials, she made him a heavy coat with help from his older sister.
The handmade jacket became a family keepsake.
Mike spent about three weeks at a Florida refugee camp before being sent to Wilmington, Delaware, where he enrolled in high school despite not speaking English.
"You do learn the language very quickly when you’re immersed in it," Mike said, recalling how his grades improved as he learned English.

"He had an enormous amount of grit and determination," Jeff said. "He had incredibly kind and supportive people who guided him all along the way.
"My dad’s story really shows that people help each other," he added.
Mike concluded the video saying, "I look back on my life, and I had lived the American dream 30 years ago. It’s just really out of this world."
